newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt offers its help in Israel-PLO peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers its help in Israel-PLO peace talks.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Monday phoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and offered to help conclude peace talks between the Jewish state and the Palestinians over the West Bank city of Hebron.
"The Egyptian president offered help in concluding negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians," a statement from Netanyahu's office said.

"Prime Minister Netanyahu said that the Egyptians can make a positive contribution to concluding negotiations, and he expected that Egypt would encourage the Palestinians to adopt a realistic and responsible position in negotiations."

Talks between Israel and the PLO with Egyptian and U.S. mediation have failed so far to bring the two sides closer to an agreement on implementing a deal signed by Israel's previous government for a partial Israeli withdrawal from Hebron.
Hebron is the last of seven major West Bank cities Israel agreed to hand over to PLO under a self-rule accord signed last year.
The Hebron pullback has been delayed by Israeli demands for better security arrangements for about 400 Jewish settlers who live or study in Hebron amidst more than 100,000 Palestinians.
